newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australian 10-yr bond holds 93.500 support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australian 10-yr bond holds 93.500 support.

text.p: *Australian bond futures ended after hours trade with modest gains over Wednesday's pit close after holding above the psychological 93.500 level on the 10-year bond contract.
*Quarterly average weekly earnings at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond futures ended after hours trade with modest gains over Wednesday's pit close after holding above the psychological 93.500 level on the 10-year bond contract.

However, the upside proved equally limited after rebounding from this session low, stalling at 93.570 and short of the 3-1/2 year 93.595 peak which was set after Wednesday's release of an extemely subdued second quarter inflation report.
Some analysts feel the contract's strong rally since April is beginning to show signs of strain with an expected policy easing already factored in at the short-end of the curve.

Until the Reserve Bank endorses a 50 basis point rate in official 5.5 percent interest rate, or when the market is fully confident that such a move is on the cards, a test of the all time peak of 93.630 on the 10-year contract may be unlikely.
The possibility of an easing may gather more momentum when second quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings data are released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).

Forecasts centre on 0.8 percent quarterly rise, which would take the annual rate down to 4.1 percent from 4.3 percent in the previous quarter, remaining below the RBA's 4.5 percent 'line in the sand'.
Treasurer Peter Costello said in a radio interview on Thursday that the RBA would take wages data into account in any decision on official interest rates.

Also holding back the local long end in after hours trade was a softer U.S. Treasury market, which succumbed to some profit-taking after Tuesday's heady advance on the first leg of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
In the second stage of his testimony on Wednesday, Greenspan said that while U.S. prices have come down, he saw no signs of the economy about to enter a period of deflation.
